name: Trillium Arts Individual Artist Residencies 2027
feeCondition: Applying is free. An optional mentorship add-on costs $75.
award: $700 honorarium and a seven-night stay in a private suite in Mars Hill, NC
eligibility: Artists 21 and older at any stage of their career; applicants outside the US cover their own travel and visa costs.
note: A week of quiet studio time in the Blue Ridge Mountains. Applying is free; an optional mentorship add-on costs $75.

name: Audible Emerging Playwrights Fund
award: Up to five commissions of $25,000 each to write and develop an original audio play
eligibility: Self-identified emerging playwrights 18 or older living in the US or UK. Submit one full-length original script, a bio of up to 300 words and a pitch for a new audio play (action and adventure or general fiction preferred).
note: Closes November 18 at 11:59 PM Eastern. One submission per person; revised resubmissions are not accepted. If you are selected, Audible's commission contract takes exclusive worldwide audio rights to the play, so read it before signing.

name: Trillium Arts "Miss Sarah" Fellowship for Black Women Writers
award: $1,000 stipend, a ten-day solo residency with housing, a rental car, and US travel covered
eligibility: Black women writers at any stage of their career; the 2027 fellowship focuses on nonfiction.
note: A July residency near Asheville, NC. Theses, dissertations and edited collections are not eligible.

name: Writers of the Future Contest (Q1 2027)
award: $1,000, $750 and $500 each quarter, plus a $5,000 annual grand prize
eligibility: Writers who haven't professionally published a novel, more than one novelette, or more than three short stories. Science fiction, fantasy or light horror up to 17,000 words; AI-generated work is not accepted.
note: A long-running quarterly contest judged anonymously by professional writers. Entrants keep all publication rights.
disclaimer: Started by L. Ron Hubbard and sponsored by Galaxy Press, the publisher of his fiction. Some writers avoid it because of its ties to the Church of Scientology, which Hubbard founded; the contest says it has no connection to the church.

name: Steinbeck Fellowship (San José State University)
award: $15,000 stipend for a one-year fellowship
eligibility: Emerging writers of fiction, drama, creative nonfiction or biography (no poetry); fellows must live in the San Francisco Bay Area or nearby counties during the fellowship and not be enrolled in a degree program.
note: Relocation required. The official form gives the deadline as "January 4" every year without naming the year; confirm before applying.

name: Poetry magazine
award: $500 per poem; prose $400 per published page
eligibility: Previously unpublished, human-written poetry, translations and prose on poetry; work posted online counts as published.
note: Free to submit. Closed every year from June 15 to September 15.

name: Rattle
award: $200 per poem in print, $100 per poem online
eligibility: Unpublished poems, translations and book reviews; up to four poems at a time. Poems posted on your own social media or blog are fine.
note: Open year-round and always free. Rights revert to the author on publication. Work mostly generated by AI is not accepted.

name: The Baltimore Review
feeCondition: Regular submissions are free. Its contests charge entry fees.
award: $75 per accepted piece
eligibility: Writers 18 and older.
note: Regular submissions are free; only its contests charge fees.

name: The Hudson Review (fiction)
award: Publication; pay not stated
eligibility: Writers of any age, background or publication history, US or international; unpublished stories under 10,000 words. No simultaneous submissions.
note: Fiction reads September 1 to November 30, online or by mail. No submission fees.

name: The Yale Review (nonfiction)
feeCondition: Nonfiction is free. Poetry submissions cost $3.
award: $250 to $1,000 for prose, depending on length
eligibility: Unpublished nonfiction in English, including pitches; previously posted work (blogs, Substack) doesn't qualify.
note: Nonfiction is free to submit by email. Poetry submissions charge $3, so this listing covers nonfiction only.

name: Redivider (Emerson College)
award: Publication; pay not stated
eligibility: Anyone except current Emerson students, faculty and staff (graduates wait three years); unpublished work.
note: Fiction, flash, poetry, memoir, cultural critique and cover art. Authors keep copyright.

name: Guernica
award: Publication; pay not stated for general submissions
eligibility: Unpublished fiction (2,000–7,000 words), nonfiction (2,500+ words) and poetry (up to five poems).
note: A respected magazine of art and politics. Poems are exclusive to Guernica for 90 days, then non-exclusive.

name: The Offing
award: $25 to $100 on publication
eligibility: Unpublished work. Open departments right now are Fiction (stories up to 7,500 words, or up to five flash pieces of 1,000 words or less) and Art & Comics (art writing, graphic prose or comics).
note: Free to submit through 2026, thanks to donors; the magazine has not said whether 2027 will be free. Departments open and close through the year, and only the ones shown on the page are reading. AI-assisted work is generally not accepted.

name: Sierra Nevada Review
award: Publication; pay not stated
eligibility: Unpublished poetry, fiction and nonfiction; one submission per reading period. Writers keep all rights.
note: The University of Nevada, Reno at Lake Tahoe journal, reading for its Spring 2027 issue.

name: Michigan Quarterly Review: MQR Online
feeCondition: MQR Online is free. Its prizes charge entry fees.
award: $50 per published piece
eligibility: Pitches for essays, book reviews, arts and culture features and author interviews; selected pitches are invited to submit up to 3,000 words.
note: Online pitches are free year-round. The prizes charge entry fees, so use the MQR Online category.

name: Barrelhouse: newsletter essays
award: $50 on publication
eligibility: Unpublished personal essays about a pop-culture obsession, under 1,000 words (strict).
note: Accepted on a rolling basis but may pause when the queue fills. Rights return to the author after the newsletter goes out. No AI-written work.

name: The Playwrights Realm: Scratchpad Series
award: A developmental workshop of up to one week in New York City with professional collaborators. Playwrights based outside New York get travel and housing or a per diem.
eligibility: Early-career playwrights from anywhere in the country; one script per writer each year. You must be able to be in New York City for 3 to 6 days during the 2027–28 season.
note: Applications close December 7 at 11:59 PM Eastern. The same page offers a Writing Fellowship, which is only for writers living within commuting distance of Midtown Manhattan.

name: Theatre503 International Playwriting Award
award: £6,000 (£3,000 in prize money plus a £3,000 advance against 8% of gross box office), a production at Theatre503 in London, and publication by Samuel French
eligibility: Writers over 16 anywhere in the world who have not had a full-length play run professionally for four weeks or more. One script in English with a cast of six or fewer; no adaptations or musicals. Scripts written or translated with generative AI are not accepted.
note: Closes at midnight UK time on January 31, 2027, so send it a day early to be safe. The winner gives Theatre503 an exclusive licence to produce the play for up to 18 months.

name: Heartland Theatre 10-Minute Play Festival
award: Winning plays are staged June 3–19, 2027 in Normal, Illinois. No payment to playwrights is stated.
eligibility: Original ten-minute plays on the 2027 theme, "Book Club". Read the theatre's "How to Submit Your Play" rules for cast and format limits before sending.
note: A long-running annual festival at a community theatre in central Illinois. The page says "No Submission Fees".

name: Vivid Stage: full-length play submissions
award: Consideration for the May "Meet the Artist" reading series and for mainstage production. Royalties are paid for readings and productions; amounts are not stated.
eligibility: One full-length comedy or drama per writer, on a contemporary topic, with a cast of eight or fewer. No musicals, period pieces, plays under 60 minutes, or AI-generated material.
note: Closed early: by November 18, 2026 its page said the 300-script limit for this season had been reached. This season's window opened November 1.

name: Sillerman First Book Prize for African Poets
award: $1,000 and book publication by the University of Nebraska Press
eligibility: Poets who were born in Africa, are nationals or residents of an African country, or have African parents, and who have not yet published a poetry collection. Manuscripts must be in English.
note: Run by the African Poetry Book Fund. US residents who meet the definition above can enter.

name: Leon Levy Center for Biography Fellowships (2027–28)
award: $72,000 stipend and writing space at the CUNY Graduate Center in New York
eligibility: Writers working on a biography, with preference for those who have not yet published one. Memoir and fiction are not eligible. Two references required. Fellows are in residence in New York from September to May.
note: Tick the box on the same form to be considered for the David Levering Lewis Fellowship, for biographies about the African Diaspora.

name: Sony World Photography Awards 2027
award: Series: $25,000, a solo exhibition and Sony camera equipment. Single Image: $5,000, Sony camera equipment and a place in the London exhibition.
eligibility: Photographers anywhere, at any career stage, shooting on any device. A Series entry is five to ten images per category.
note: Single Image entries close January 5, 2027 and Series entries close January 12, both at 4 PM UK time (11 AM Eastern). Read the terms before entering: they give the organizers a licence to use entered images to promote the awards.

name: SmokeLong Quarterly Emerging Writer Fellowship (January–June 2027)
award: Six months reading submissions alongside the editors, free access to the SmokeLong Fitness workshop, and monthly feedback from senior editors. No cash award.
eligibility: Writers 18 or older who have not published a book-length work of fiction or nonfiction. Expect 5 to 7 hours a week of reading. Apply with three flash pieces under 1,000 words each and a 300-word statement.
note: For writers of flash fiction and flash nonfiction. Closes December 15 at midnight New York time.

name: Pulitzer Center Global Reporting Grants
award: Travel and reporting costs for a reporting project. The center says most international travel awards are $5,000 to $10,000.
eligibility: Staff and freelance journalists in any country, including photographers, audio and video journalists and documentary filmmakers. Proposals should include letters of interest or commitment from outlets that plan to publish the work.
note: There is no deadline: grants are awarded on a rolling basis, and editors reply within two or three weeks. The grant covers reporting costs, not pay; the center expects outlets to pay journalists for their work.

name: The Sun (photography)
feeCondition: Photography submissions are free. The Sun's writing submissions charge $2.50.
award: Payment on publication; the amount is not stated on the submissions page.
eligibility: Black-and-white photographs, up to 30 at a time, sent through the magazine's online form. Email submissions are not accepted.
note: The Sun publishes black-and-white photography and tries to reply to each submission within a month.

name: The Aftermath Project Post-Conflict Grant 2026
award: $25,000 grant; four finalists are also named.
eligibility: Working photographers anywhere in the world with a project about the aftermath of conflict. Full-time students are not eligible.
note: Proposals go by email with a file-sharing link and close at midnight Pacific time on December 1. No budget is needed.

name: Surel's Place Artist Residency
award: About a month living and working in a private home in Boise, Idaho.
eligibility: Artists 25 and older working in visual, literary or other media. Fiction is not being considered in this cycle.
note: The March 1 deadline is for residencies from July to December 2027; the next deadline, September 1, is for January to June 2028. The application page does not mention a stipend.

name: Wergle Flomp Humor Poetry Contest
award: $2,000 first prize; ten honorable mentions of $200 each.
eligibility: One humor poem of up to 250 lines, in English. Open to poets in most countries, with no age limit.
note: The page says "No fee to enter." Winners give a nonexclusive licence to publish the poem online and keep all other rights.
aiPolicy: Entries must be written without AI.

name: Treehouse Climate Action Poem Prize 2027 (Academy of American Poets)
award: $1,000, $750, $500 and $250 prizes; all four winning poems appear in Poem-a-Day.
eligibility: US citizens, people who have lived in the US for the ten years before the deadline, and DACA or TPS holders. One previously unpublished poem.
note: A prize for poems about climate change. The guidelines say "There is no entry fee."

name: Jim Baen Memorial Short Story Award
award: Grand prize: publication on the Baen Books website at its normal rate, currently 8 cents a word. Second and third places get conference entry and National Space Society membership.
eligibility: Original, unpublished stories in English of up to 8,000 words about near-future human space exploration, from writers in any country.
note: Entries go by email as an RTF file and close at 12:01 AM Pacific on February 1, 2027. The page says "No entry fee."

name: Philip Roth Residence in Creative Writing (Bucknell University)
award: $5,000 stipend and housing in Bucknell's Poets' Cottage for up to four months, in fall 2027 or spring 2028.
eligibility: Writers working on a first or second book in any literary genre.
note: A residency at Bucknell University in Pennsylvania. No fee is mentioned on the residency page.

name: The Leah Playwriting Prize 2027
award: $5,000, plus a public reading and summer workshop at Vassar College's Powerhouse Theater in 2027.
eligibility: Emerging women, trans and non-binary playwrights anywhere in the world, with one completed full-length play in English.
note: Closes December 15 or as soon as 400 applications arrive, whichever comes first. The page says "There is no fee to apply."

name: Jerome Fellowship 2027–29 (Playwrights' Center)
award: $25,000 a year for two years as a part-time employee with health insurance, plus $3,000 a year for play development.
eligibility: Playwrights over 18 with the legal right to work in the US and no more than two professionally produced plays. Fellows must live in Minnesota from July 2027 to June 2029; housing and travel are not provided.
note: Closes December 3 at 11:59 PM Central. One application now covers both the Jerome and Many Voices fellowships.

name: Many Voices Fellowship 2027–29 (Playwrights' Center)
award: $25,000 a year for two years as a part-time employee with health insurance, plus $3,000 a year for play development.
eligibility: Early-career Black playwrights, playwrights of color and Indigenous playwrights over 18, with the legal right to work in the US and no more than two professionally produced plays. Fellows must live in Minnesota from July 2027 to June 2029; housing and travel are not provided.
note: Closes December 3 at 11:59 PM Central. One application now covers both the Many Voices and Jerome fellowships.

name: The Drift
award: $500 to $1,000 per short story; $150 per poem.
eligibility: Fiction and poetry sent by email following the magazine's guidelines; poets may submit no more than twice a year.
note: Submissions go by email with no stated reading period, and no fee is mentioned. Nonfiction writers send a pitch first.
aiPolicy: Work written by AI is not accepted.

name: Clarkesworld Magazine
award: 14 cents a word for fiction; 10 cents a word for nonfiction; $450 for cover art.
eligibility: Science fiction and fantasy stories of 1,000 to 22,000 words, in English, from writers anywhere. No simultaneous submissions and no horror.
note: The submissions page says it is "currently open" for stories, nonfiction and art. Fiction buys first world electronic and print rights plus non-exclusive anthology rights.
aiPolicy: Work written or made by AI is not accepted.

name: Foundation for Contemporary Arts Emergency Grants
award: $500 to $3,000 toward costs tied to a confirmed upcoming presentation of your work.
eligibility: Individual artists living in the US or its territories, with a US tax ID and a confirmed exhibition or performance date. Students in degree programs are not eligible.
note: Open year-round. Apply 8 to 10 weeks before the presentation date, and no earlier than 10 weeks.

name: The Orchard Project Episodic Lab 2027
award: A six-week virtual writers' room in late summer 2027 with script and pitch notes from industry professionals. No stipend is stated.
eligibility: Anyone writing a TV pilot, with no age limit and no agent needed; most participants have shown creative work in public before. Takes part online from anywhere.
note: Closes at 11:59 PM Eastern on January 3, 2027. The page says "Apply for free by January 3."
